run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation application is failing on the /hotels page: frontend returns HTTP 500, and the failure chain visible in traces is frontend -> search -> rate, where rate is shedding load through its own admission-control queue. rate's own metrics report rate_backend_qps_limit=20, rate_queue_capacity=256 with rate_queue_depth=256 (queue exactly at capacity), rate_requests_rejected_total=485 and rate_requests_expired_total=141 against rate_requests_received_total=1237 and only 496 completed (evidence 7f580374-04fb-4cc3-972a-6e95b0b3ff92-t0:f1c84a1d-4dd6-403d-9f7a-a71bb04486b4). Sampled rate /rate.Rate/GetRates server spans take about 12.78-12.80 s (queue capacity 256 / 20 QPS = 12.8 s) while other rate spans fail immediately in 14-35 us (57614485-0539-464a-b50d-2d3053c229f7-t0:21fd35c8-4091-4d52-9ddd-cd5c7f929399). search's own logs name the dependency explicitly: 'downstream request failed dependency=rate grpc_code=ResourceExhausted' and 'grpc_code=DeadlineExceeded' (7bb17419-a99c-4027-a672-0c966b478a46-t0:e7ffd5d3-7dfc-4e46-9f4f-fc9a299424fa), and its counters show timeouts rising 16 -> 1447 and failures 0 -> 755 while successes stayed at 355 (7f580374-04fb-4cc3-972a-6e95b0b3ff92-t1:e8358838-f2a3-495f-92f1-c5c36a118a0d). The two settings that carry this behaviour sit on the rate Deployment (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256); the search Deployment additionally sets a 750 ms rate RPC deadline with 3 retry attempts, which converts the 12.8 s queueing into immediate DeadlineExceeded and amplifies offered load. Pods and dependencies are otherwise healthy: all 19 pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts, no CPU throttling or memory limits, and mongodb-rate logs are clean. The conclusion is partial because the whole namespace was created at 04:30:15-04:30:27 (no pre-incident baseline), the change-history integration is not available, and I did not see the setting being changed nor measure rate's backend latency or the offered QPS directly.

claims.text: All 19 pods in namespace hotel-reservation are Running and ready with restart count 0, owned by their ReplicaSets, with start times between 04:30:15Z and 04:30:27Z on 2026-11-24; no pod shows a last termination reason or exit code.

The rate Deployment rate (ReplicaSet rate-c4d7bcb48, created 04:30:16Z, generation 1) and the search Deployment search (ReplicaSet search-7769dfc66b, created 04:30:17Z, generation 1) each have exactly one ReplicaSet and one pod; the workloads were deployed once at the start of the observed period, with no second ReplicaSet indicating an in-window config rollout.

The rate Deployment container hotel-reserv-rate carries env RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 (plus JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1); the search Deployment container hotel-reserv-search carries RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS=50, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER=2.0 and RATE_RPC_JITTER=0.2.

Across all 19 Deployments in hotel-reservation, the only rate-limiter / RPC-policy variables are on rate (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY) and search (RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER, RATE_RPC_JITTER); every other application Deployment carries only JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO or no env at all.

rate's own metrics at 04:31:30Z-04:32:15Z report rate_backend_qps_limit=20, rate_queue_capacity=256, rate_queue_depth=256 (queue exactly full), rate_requests_received_total=1237, rate_requests_completed_total=496, rate_requests_rejected_total=485, rate_requests_expired_total=141 and rate_in_flight=0 (instance rate.hotel-reservation:9091).

search's own metrics sampled at 04:31:30Z vs 04:32:15Z moved as follows: search_rate_attempts_total 415 -> 2655, search_rate_timeouts_total 16 -> 1447, search_rate_failures_total 0 -> 755, search_rate_successes_total 355 -> 355 (unchanged), search_requests_total 401 -> 1128 (instance search.hotel-reservation:9092).

Sampled traces show the failing chain with exact identities: frontend server span 'HTTP GET /hotels' with error=true, http.status_code=500, otel.status_code=ERROR (duration 899115-2425519 us); its child frontend client span '/search.Search/Nearby' with error=true; the search service's own '/search.Search/Nearby' server span with error=true; and search's child client span '/rate.Rate/GetRates' with error=true at 750661 us.

In the same sampled traces, rate's own '/rate.Rate/GetRates' server spans split into two populations: uniformly about 12.78-12.80 s spans with no status tag (spans 3ef97f28bcd8d425, 0c79166f49cbcbac, 733702e9cc2d7412) and very short failing spans of 14-35 us with error=true (spans 267ca42cb31ef178, 1586ae6e37014b8f, 3fff4eea79c24ab3).

search pod search-7769dfc66b-5sw7s logged 789 matching warning lines in the window, all naming rate as the failing dependency: 'services/search/server.go:252 > downstream request failed dependency=rate grpc_code=ResourceExhausted' and 'dependency=rate grpc_code=DeadlineExceeded', from 04:32:08Z through 04:32:15Z.

At the moment of the alert query (04:34, after the window) the alerting rule HighRequestLatency was firing for labels service_name=rate, namespace=hotel-reservation with activeAt 2026-11-24T04:32:26Z and value 10000 ms (P95 threshold 3000 ms over a 2m span-metric window), and HighRequestErrorRate was pending for service_name=frontend (0.8223) and service_name=search (0.6007) with activeAt 04:33:26Z.

The cluster events in the window contain no failure-reason events for hotel-reservation: only Normal Scheduling/Created/Pulled/Started events for the 19 pods and ScalingReplicaSet/SuccessfulCreate for the Deployments and ReplicaSets; no Killing, OOMKilling, Evicted, Unhealthy, FailedMount or FailedScheduling events appear in that namespace (those appear only in other namespaces such as observe, openebs and kube-system).

The only ConfigMaps in hotel-reservation are kube-root-ca.crt and the two MongoDB init scripts mongo-geo-script and mongo-rate-script; there is no fault-injection or feature-flag ConfigMap in the namespace.

Resource pressure does not explain rate's behaviour: container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total is 0 for both the hotel-reserv-rate and hotel-reserv-search containers, rate used 1.80 s CPU cumulative with about 20.4 MB working set, no memory limit is set (container_spec_memory_limit_bytes=0 for these containers), and no throttling appears on the pod-level series either.

rate's MongoDB dependency showed no failure in the window: mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-8h28l logged normal startup, connection accepted, successful SCRAM authentication on principalName admin, index build on rate-db.inventory and a WiredTiger checkpoint at 04:31:26Z, with no error or slow-query lines in the lines read.

The other dependency of the failing /hotels path, geo, was not failing: in trace 677b8b4fd354a2d4 the search-side '/geo.Geo/Nearby' client span completed in 739 us and the geo server span in 33 us, both without an error status tag.

The rate pod itself started cleanly: hotel-reserv-rate logged reading mongodb-rate:27017, memcached-rate:11211, port 8084, jaeger agent, 'Read profile memcashed address: memcached-rate:11211' and 'Successfully registered in consul' for srv-rate at 04:30:26Z, with 24 log lines and no error lines after startup.

The frontend pod's only error lines were startup-time Consul discovery failures at 04:30:16Z-04:30:17Z ('error retrieving instances from Consul ... dial tcp 10.96.196.20:8500: connect: connection refused' for srv-search, srv-profile and srv-recommendation), i.e. a startup race before Consul was reachable, not a persisted runtime dependency failure in the 04:31-04:32 sampling period.

Primary explanation consistent with every observation: the rate Deployment's admission control (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 serving capacity with RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256) is the binding constraint - the queue sits exactly at capacity, 626 of 1237 received requests (485 rejected + 141 expired) never complete, admitted requests wait about 12.8 s (256/20) before service, and callers therefore receive ResourceExhausted and DeadlineExceeded from dependency=rate, which surfaces as frontend HTTP 500 on GET /hotels.

Second candidate, not yet excluded: the search Deployment's RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750 with RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 and exponential backoff turns rate's queue latency into immediate caller-visible errors and multiplies offered load (search_rate_attempts_total rose to 2655 against search_requests_total 1128), so it is at least an amplifier of the incident even if not its origin.

Third candidate, not yet excluded: rate logged 'Generating test data...' at 04:30:26Z right after start, so initial cold-start/backfill work may have contributed to the early backlog; this cannot explain the saturation still visible at 04:32Z on its own and its weight is unmeasured.

Validate the diagnosis against a baseline before changing anything: raise or remove RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT (and adjust rate_queue_capacity) on the rate Deployment, or reduce the offered request rate, then confirm that rate_requests_rejected_total and rate_requests_expired_total stop increasing, rate P95 latency falls below the 1500 ms target, and frontend GET /hotels stops returning 500.

Separately review search's retry policy (RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 with RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750): retrying a queue-saturated dependency triples its load, and a single attempt with a deadline above the expected queue wait, or circuit breaking, would avoid converting rate queueing into a 500 at the frontend.

gaps: No pre-incident baseline exists: every hotel-reservation pod and Deployment was created at 04:30:15-04:30:27Z inside the window (first rate_* sample 04:31:30Z, first search_* sample 04:31:15Z), so rate's latency and error levels before the failure cannot be compared and the deviation cannot be quantified.

Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, and the rate and search Deployments show generation 1 / revision 1 with a single ReplicaSet each, so I cannot tell whether RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 were deliberately injected, when they were set, or what the previous values were.

Rate-of-change queries over the rate_* and search_* counters returned no data (increase()/rate() views eeb056f0-51e9-4b91-8efb-3a827297acc7-t0:31d73dd5-85d7-4d30-8736-f619e2332bb1, e3da7ea0-5378-424c-8496-0d198afa91d6-t0:f90f8722-6f7a-4e34-ac2e-8c2423080057, e3da7ea0-5378-424c-8496-0d198afa91d6-t1:6039bb1f-64b1-4755-b8a1-074d0b5fe83b and 8fc10e94-4497-4f32-8753-f779737c4449-t0:53dec244-522a-491e-87e1-3271ab96952b all reported no data), so the offered request rate and per-second rejection/timeout rates could not be computed; the numbers reported are sampled cumulative values at 04:31:30Z and 04:32:15Z.

rate's backend latency was not measured: traces_search for service 'rate' was rejected with INVALID_PARAMS because that service is not in the permitted list, and no mongo_rate or memcached span durations for service rate were returned, so whether mongodb-rate or memcached-rate adds latency to the admitted requests is unknown.

No complete slow trace was observed: traces_query_trace_by_id for trace 677b8b4fd354a2d4 reported 10 spans lying outside the query window that were not shown, so the full 12.8 s rate path (including its mongo/memcached child spans) is only partially visible; the read slice 57614485-0539-464a-b50d-2d3053c229f7-t0:21fd35c8-4091-4d52-9ddd-cd5c7f929399 is itself truncated (140 of 271 rows).

Checked and found nothing, therefore unverified rather than healthy: traces_search_by_tags with error=true returned no data for profile (de9a2f10-9014-4188-b544-5302e1554998-t0:ec2f4b99-61d8-4413-93d5-02df883345bb) and for reservation (de9a2f10-9014-4188-b544-5302e1554998-t1:8885d125-61ae-4375-b338-389db4d7f24b); absence in a sampled view cannot certify those services are unaffected.

The error=false / mongo_rate trace filters (b4040e94-1555-4453-ae71-80a65102efb1-t0:d3774761-9e35-437b-b209-3336a45d3e39 and b4040e94-1555-4453-ae71-80a65102efb1-t1:329b8229-b631-4939-85b9-2d9af91b9435) matched nothing, so the successful rate path has no supporting sample and success-side latency remains unknown.

The rate and search metric series were not among the metric-name listing filters I successfully used for the 'http_/rpc_/app_' pattern (f2e559fd-04d3-4f6a-b424-c1a70a9cde24-t1:c731ca7d-da15-41c0-ad3b-5429c74fde58 returned no data for that pattern), so no additional application-level error metric beyond traces_span_metrics_calls_total and the rate_*/search_* counters was reviewed.

No firing ALERTS series was returned by the direct ALERTS query (b5d51566-6bde-414f-8f0d-54d1e66d4007-t0:178d6e35-7662-47fe-bbbe-abdc23028f83, no data); the alert state reported comes only from the rule listing taken after the window.
Secrets could not be read, so any credential-dependent behaviour (MongoDB credentials, memcached settings) was not verified.

Whether frontend users were affected beyond the /hotels page is unverified: only 'HTTP GET /hotels' 500 spans were observed, and the other frontend operations (/profile.Profile/GetProfiles, /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability) were not sampled in this analysis.
next_steps: Compare the current rate and search Deployment env values against the intended application manifest or version control to confirm whether RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 are the injected fault rather than the intended baseline.
Measure rate's dependency latency (mongo_rate and memcached_get_multi_rate span durations for service rate) to fully separate queue-wait time from backend service time.

Reproduce under a controlled load and record rate_queue_depth, rate_requests_rejected_total and search_rate_timeouts_total over several minutes to confirm the 256/20 = 12.8 s queue-drain explanation and to size a correct limit.

Collect a longer pre-incident baseline for rate P95 latency and frontend /hotels error rate once the namespace has been up longer, to quantify the deviation instead of relying on single-snapshot counters.

No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

query.jq_expr: .items | map({kind: .involvedObject.kind, namespace: .involvedObject.namespace, reason}) | group_by(.) | .[] | .[0] + {count: length}

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. #!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
